newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sucden plans 400,000 T Russia 97 raw sugar imports.
newsitem.headline: Sucden plans 400,000 T Russia 97 raw sugar imports.

text.p: Sucden-Moskva, a major importer of Cuban raw sugar into Russia, plans to import 400,000 tonnes of raws in 1997 against around 250,000 tonnes in 1996, a company official was quoted by Prime-Tass news agency as saying Tuesday.
Company officials in Moscow were not able to confirm the figure.

Sucden-Moskva, part of French sugar group Sucden Kerry, told Tass it did not intend to increase the amount of sugar it imported to Russia this year beyond 400,000 tonnes, despite a rise in sugar prices on Russia's domestic market.
The official said loading capacity limits at Russian ports was a constraining factor, as was the high cost of transporting sugar by sea.

He said the company was continuing to deliver equipment to a sugar refinery being built in the Stavropol, in southern Russia, under a contract won by Sucden Kerry and FCB, the engineering unit of Fives-Lille, in December 1994.
Last year a total of $120 million worth of equipment was delivered to the factory, Tass said.

The refinery was due to be completed by the end of 1997 and would have an initial daily sugar beet processing capacity of 6,000 tonnes, possibly rising to 9,000 tonnes. --Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
